Bank Of Hawaii Has Cut Monsanto Co (MON) Position as Valuation Rose; Apple (AAPL) Holding Has Boosted by Vantage Investment Partners Llc
June 10, 2018 - By Adrian Mccoy
Bank Of Hawaii decreased its stake in Monsanto Co (MON) by 27.44% Bank Of Hawaii sold 3,569 shares as the company’s stock rose 2.93% while stock markets declined. The institutional investor held 9,438 shares of the agricultural chemicals $1.10M, down from 13,007 Bank Of Hawaii who had been investing in Monsanto Co $56.46 billion market cap company. The stock increased 0.02% or $0.02 $127.95. About 7.06 million shares traded or 55.81% up from the average. Monsanto Company (NYSE:MON) has risen 8.56% since June 10, 2017 and is uptrending. It has underperformed by 4.01% the S&P500. Vantage Investment Partners Llc increased its stake in Apple Inc (AAPL) by 888.26% Vantage Investment Partners Llc bought 87,520 shares as the company’s stock rose 5.37% while stock markets declined. The institutional investor held 97,373 shares of the computer manufacturing $16.34M, up from 9,853 Vantage Investment Partners Llc who had been investing in Apple Inc for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $942.23B market cap company. The stock decreased 0.91% or $1.76 $191.7. About 26.47M shares traded. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has risen 22.56% since June 10, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 9.99% the S&P500. Bank Of Hawaii, which manages about $1.30 billion and $1.20B US Long portfolio, upped its stake in Ishares (EFA) by 42,194 shares to 53,518 shares, valued at $3.73M in 2018Q1, according to the filing. It also increased its holding in Public Storage Inc (NYSE:PSA) by 2,398 shares in the quarter, for a total of 4,864 shares, and has risen its stake in Vanguard (VWO).
Analysts await Monsanto Company (NYSE:MON) to report earnings on June, 27. They expect $2.19 EPS, up 13.47% or $0.26 from last year’s $1.93 per share. MON’s profit will be $966.41M for 14.61 P/E if the $2.19 EPS becomes a reality. After $3.22 actual EPS reported by Monsanto Company for the previous quarter, Wall Street now forecasts -31.99% negative EPS growth.
